title: Runtime upgrade validation and canary matrix
author: Emily Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable, telemetry-driven validation matrix and automated canary procedure for runtime component upgrades (kernels, schedulers, KV-cache variants, and compilation artifacts). It combines benchmark gating, live-canary thresholds, and automated rollback criteria to reduce risk while enabling faster iteration.

Scope: applies to server-side runtime components deployed to hosted and dedicated environments. Excludes customer-managed Private deployments unless explicitly opted into Redwood upgrade automation.

Audience: runtime engineers, infra SRE, release managers, product reliability.

Goals

- Standardize evidence required before a kernel/scheduler change is promoted.
- Automate canary progression based on concrete telemetry signals.
- Provide clear, reproducible rollback gates to prevent production regressions.

Key definitions

- Candidate: A build artifact (kernel binary, scheduler config, quantized weights + kernel hints) targeted for rollout.
- Canary cohort: Fraction of traffic routed to candidate.
- Validation matrix: Cross-product of workload classes and required checks (benchmarks, profiling, live SLOs).

Validation matrix (summary table)

Workload class | Benchmarks required | Profiling artifacts | Live telemetry thresholds
---------------|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------
Light chat (seq <= 128) | microbench p50/p95 throughput, token-per-second | kernel traces, occupancy profile | p95 latency delta <= +10ms, error rate delta <= +0.05% absolute
Long-form gen (seq 512–4096) | tail-latency simulation, memory growth test | allocation flamegraph, KV-cache hit-ratio | p99 latency delta <= +15%, OOM events == 0
High-concurrency embeddings | throughput-saturation, queuing model test | concurrency contention traces | throughput delta >= -7%, queue length growth <= 15%
Cold-start heavy | cold-start latency benchmark | warmup hit-rate and init-cost trace | cold-start p95 delta <= +25% of baseline

Pre-flight checklist (CI / bench stage)

1) Automated performance benchmarks complete and pass thresholds in isolated test harness (see matrix above).
2) Profiling artifacts uploaded to internal profiling store: kernel traces, NVidia counters, KV-cache hit heatmaps.
3) Static analysis and safety checks: no non-deterministic memory accesses reported; sanitizers pass on debug builds.
4) Automated canary plan generated (JSON) with target filters (model families, customer tiers, regions). Example plan snippet:

{
  "candidate": "kernel-v2.3.1",
  "cohorts": [{"pct": 1, "duration_min": 60}, {"pct": 5, "duration_min": 30}, {"pct": 20, "duration_min": 30}, {"pct": 50, "duration_min": 60}],
  "gates": {"p95_latency_pct": 110, "error_rate_absolute": 0.0005}
}

(Above JSON is illustrative; CI generates canonical plan stored at "/releases/runtime/canary-plans/<candidate>.json")

Live canary progression policy

- Start: 1% traffic for 60 minutes. Collect signals from telemetry backend.
- Metrics evaluated: latency p50/p95/p99, request error rate, kernel-level metrics (warp occupancy, SM utilization), GPU memory fragmentation events, KV-cache hit ratio, GC/alloc stalls.
- Evaluation windows: rolling 5m and 30m windows. Candidate must satisfy both short and mid windows.
- Progression: If all gates pass for the mid window, advance to next cohort. Otherwise hold for remediation and re-evaluate after operator intervention.

Automated gating thresholds (default)

- p95 latency: candidate <= baseline * 1.10 (10% relative increase allowed)
- p99 latency: candidate <= baseline * 1.15
- Error rate (4xx/5xx): absolute increase <= 0.05% (0.0005)
- OOM / GPU watchdog events: 0 allowed
- Memory growth (over 2h): <= 5% relative
- Kernel launch failures: 0 allowed

Custom gates per change type

- Kernel micro-optimizations: tighten p95 to 1.05 and require occupancy within 3% of baseline.
- Scheduler policy changes: require queue-length regression < 10% and throughput regression < 5%.
- Quantization / compilation changes: require accuracy-preserving regressions flagged in model-evaluations <= acceptable threshold (team-specific).

Rollback criteria and automation

1) If any hard gate (OOM, kernel-launch-failure, watchdog) triggers, immediately abort canary and trigger rollback automation to previous stable artifact. 2) If soft gates (latency or error delta) fail consecutively for two mid-windows, pause and notify on-call and release manager. Automated snapshot of traces, flamegraphs, and sample requests is captured. 3) Rollback steps (automated):
   a) Set routing weight of candidate to 0 via traffic-controller API.
   b) Post-deploy job: restore previous kernel artifacts to nodes that had changed (idempotent).

Operational runbook (step-by-step)

1) Prepare candidate: verify CI artifacts and upload profiling bundles. 2) Create canary plan via release CLI:

$ rdeploy canary create --candidate kernel-v2.3.1 --plan /releases/runtime/canary-plans/kernel-v2.3.1.json

3) Kick off canary:

$ rdeploy canary start --candidate kernel-v2.3.1 --env prod-us-east-1

4) Monitor dashboards for the first 60 minutes. Required checks in parallel:
- Latency dashboard (p50/p95/p99)
- Error-rate heatmap by customer tier
- Kernel-level telemetry panel: warp occupancy, kernel duration histogram
- Memory fragmentation and allocation stalls panel

5) If gates pass, approve progression via CLI or UI:

$ rdeploy canary progress --candidate kernel-v2.3.1 --to 5

6) If any gate fails, abort:

$ rdeploy canary abort --candidate kernel-v2.3.1 --reason "p95 delta breach"

Observability and required dashboards

- Canary overview: candidate, cohort, routing %, evaluation status.
- Signal breakdown: latency, errors, throughput, kernel traces, memory metrics.
- Rollforward / rollback audit log.

Benchmarking hygiene

- Benchmarks must be seeded with production-like request mixes; synthetic single-query microbenchmarks are insufficient alone.
- For each candidate, attach the benchmark run id and the commit SHA to the canary plan.

Profiling artifact requirements

- Kernel traces (per-shard, per-GPU) for representative workloads; include nvprof / CUPTI counters.
- KV-cache heatmaps: hit ratio by prefix and warmup curves.
- Memory allocator profiles (jemalloc stats or equivalent).

Failure investigation checklist (if canary fails)

1) Re-run microbench with same load profile from bench harness and compare traces. 2) Capture top-N slow requests and replay in local dev cluster. 3) Check kernel/build differences (diff .cubin/.ptx metadata). 4) Inspect scheduler metrics for throttling or priority inversion. 5) If a fix requires configuration change, create a follow-up candidate and attach a root-cause summary to the original canary record.

Roles and ownership

- Runtime team: prepares candidates, ensures profiling artifacts, makes fixes.
- Infra SRE: approves global canary windows, supervises rollbacks, validates capacity.
- Release manager: coordinates cross-team communications, authorizes canary progression beyond 20% for high-risk changes.
- On-call: responds to automated alerts triggered by failed gates.

Related automation endpoints (examples)

- Traffic controller: POST /api/v1/traffic/control {candidate, weight}
- Canary controller: POST /api/v1/canary/start {candidate, plan}
- Telemetry query job: GET /api/v1/telemetry/query?query=canary_signals

Post-release requirements

- 72-hour monitoring window: run automated regression check at 24h and 72h and record results.
- Publish release note summarizing canary outcome, telemetry snippets, and any mitigations. Include links to profiling bundles.

Appendix A — Example canary plan (complete)

candidate: kernel-v2.3.1
filters:
  regions: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]
  model_tags: ["chat-light", "embeddings-small"]
  customer_tiers: ["free", "standard"]
cohorts:
  - pct: 1
    duration_min: 60
  - pct: 5
    duration_min: 30
  - pct: 20
    duration_min: 30
  - pct: 50
    duration_min: 60
gates:
  p95_latency_pct: 110
  p99_latency_pct: 115
  error_rate_absolute: 0.0005
  max_oom_events: 0

Appendix B — Example telemetry queries

- p95 latency delta (5m):
  baseline = metric("runtime.latency.p95", tag: baseline)
  candidate = metric("runtime.latency.p95", tag: candidate)
  query: 100 * (candidate / baseline)

- error-rate absolute: count(errors)/count(requests) over 5m window

Appendix C — FAQ

Q: When should we tighten gates?
A: For any change that touches memory allocation or scheduling, tighten p95 to 1.05 and require no more than 2% memory growth.

Q: Who can abort a canary?
A: On-call and Infra SRE have automated abort privileges; runtime owners and release manager should be notified immediately.

Q: Can we run a canary scoped to a single customer?
A: Yes — use customer filters in the canary plan, but for high-risk internal-only fixes prefer canarying on internal test tenants first.
